newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index hits record, Borsodchem suspended.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index hits record, Borsodchem suspended.

text.p: Hungarian shares continued their rally on Monday, driving the BUX index to the second successive daily record despite rising tension within Hungary's ruling coalition, trader said.
The BUX closed at 3,682.18 points, up 42.50, in average spot share turnover, totalling 934.3 million forints.
"Better-than-expected U.S. figures published on Friday are in the background," said MKB Securities' Peter Lencs. "An interest rate raise is not likely there and foreigners began to buy here as well."
Dealers added that the junior ruling coalition party's announcement in the weekend that the coalition may split over a privatisation scandal, did not influence investors.
Two-thirds of the share issues on the Budapest Stock Exchange rose on Monday, driven by the oil company MOL and Richter.

MOL was propelled by Prime Minister Gyula Horn's announcement on late Friday that energy prices are likely to be raised by up to 23 percent on January 1, dealers said. The stock finished at 1,745 forints, up 85.

Some investors replaced their stocks in the drug maker Egis with shares in the other pharmaceuticals company Richter as the latter was seen less sensitive to state subsidies, said Raiffeisen Securities Attila Berecz, adding that a debate was boiling over next year's subsidies.
Egis closed down by 70 forints at 9.830, while Richter firmed to 8,460 forints, up 110.
Trading in the chemicals maker Borsodchem was suspended as the subscription price at an international private placement was fixed on Monday, at $18.50/Global Depositary Receipt.
Dealers said they expected good third quarter corporate results to be published from the end of October, and this may boost the BUX index further.

Foreign investors may have neglected the sharp political clashes between the government and the opposition, and between the two parties of the ruling coalition, if the debates will continue, they may hold the prices down, dealers added.
